text:
Elaine: Quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC — thinking about pushing RBAC decisioning into the control plane for console queries. Pros/cons?

Mike: Pros: central policy management, easier canarying and rollouts, unified telemetry. Cons: adds an extra RTT for auth checks and creates a potential control-plane hotspot.

Sam: +1 on telemetry. Also can we avoid the RTT by having the control plane mint short-lived capability tokens so the data plane can validate locally?

Anika: Capability tokens are promising but need strong scoping: route prefixes, actions, ttl, and audience. Need to decide token format (JWT vs compact mac). Perf & size matter.

Raj: Also consider a hot-path cache in the data plane keyed by (tenant, route, token-hash). That reduces repeated crypto ops. Revocation semantics are going to be the hard part.

Elaine: Core tradeoff I'm weighing: inline authz in data plane (fast, replicated rules, more code duplication) vs control plane decisioning (single source, slower). How do we handle revocation windows for cached decisions?

Mike: For revocation: short token TTL + push invalidation from control plane to data plane via streaming channel. If we can't push, fall back to short TTL + accept small revocation window.

Sam: Perf angle: auth QPS to control plane could be large for high-traffic dashboards. We should design for sampling and adaptive evaluation: fully evaluate 1% and use cached policy fingerprints for the rest.

Anika: Rollout proposal: 1) Implement capability token MVP using a compact MACed token (avoid heavy JWT libs). 2) Wire data plane validation + local cache. 3) Start with 10% of routes in canary. 4) Add streaming invalidation and metrics. 5) Gradually increase coverage.

Raj: I'll take dashboard ownership for the rollout: per-route auth latency, cache hit rate, revocation lag, control-plane cpu. Set alerts on p99 auth latency > 30ms.

Mike: I'll build a perf harness to simulate 10k RPS with burstiness and measure P50/P95/P99 for the token validation path.

Sam: I'll prototype the token format and a small verifier library in Rust for the data plane path. Keep the API minimal: `X-Redwood-Cap` header with base64 token.

Anika: Security checklist: threat model for stolen tokens, replay, cross-tenant scoping. Need KMS rotation plan and key id in token header.

Elaine: Ops checklist for RFC update: dashboards (Raj), canary runbook (Mike), token spec (Sam), security review (Anika). I'll write the RFC follow-up with the proposed rollout timeline and link here.

deploy-bot: canary deployed to prod-canary at 5150013401 :rocket:

Elaine: Thanks, team — I'll draft the follow-up and tag owners. :thumbsup:
